name: Instinct
summary: Instinct is a consumer AI assistant that connects to users' apps and devices to complete tasks through text and voice interactions. Its September 2026 Series C valued it at $10 billion.
overview: Instinct is a consumer agent built to take actions across connected services. On September 28, 2026, the company announced a $1 billion Series C from Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital, and Coatue at a $10 billion valuation.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Instinct announced investments from Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital, and Coatue.

bull_case: A consumer agent that reliably executes multi-step tasks could earn a high-frequency relationship with users across multiple services.
bear_case: Consumer trust, permissions, privacy concerns, and the cost of agent execution can undermine adoption and retention.
directory_notes: Watch product reliability, user retention, and the cost of operating task-completing agents.

intelligence.description: A consumer AI assistant designed to take actions across connected applications and devices.
company: Instinct offers a personal AI assistant that users can connect to applications and devices through texts and calls, positioning it around task completion rather than only answers. The company says the agent can use its own phone number and computer to handle work such as travel planning, reservations, shopping, and subscription cancellations.

In September 2026, Instinct announced a $1 billion Series C at a $10 billion valuation from Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital, and Coatue. The completed round followed an August Series B reported at $250 million and a $2.5 billion valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Consumer agents are a high-upside but high-trust category: real task completion creates more value than a chatbot only if users grant broad access. Instinct's rapid move from a $2.5 billion Series B valuation to $10 billion in a month is a useful read-through on investor appetite for that model.

changed.text: A $250M Series B was reported at a $2.5B valuation.
Instinct announces a $1B Series C at a $10B valuation, with Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital, and Coatue investing.

takeaways: The Series C values Instinct at $10B, four times the reported Series B valuation from the prior month.
Reliable task completion and user trust are the decisive product tests.
Privacy concerns, compute costs, and competition from major platforms remain acute risks.
